prompt: This page is cited in drug-encyclopedia entries on synthetic cannabinoids, for these substances: ADB-BUTINACA. Report from the page, exactly as printed (numbers digit by digit, names in the page's own spelling and punctuation, lists complete and in page order): (1) chemical identifiers and names for each of these substances: every name used (INN, systematic, IUPAC or chemical name, other names, synonyms, abbreviations and code names), CAS number(s), molecular formula, molecular weight or molar mass, ATC code, and schedule or control status; (2) forms and products: physical forms, appearance, formulations, product types, product or brand names, packaging, and any seizure or drug-checking findings described (briefly, keeping key terms in the page's wording). Say 'not given' for anything the page does not contain. Do not add anything that is not on the page, and do not quote any passage longer than 15 words.
answer:
**(1) Chemical identifiers and names**

- **INN:** Not available
- **CAS registry numbers:** 2666932-43-8 (compound); 2682867-55-4 ((S)-enantiomer)
- **CAS name:** N-[1-(aminocarbonyl)-2,2-dimethylpropyl]-1-butyl-1H-indazole-3-carboxamide
- **IUPAC name:** N-[1-(Aminocarbonyl)-2,2-dimethylpropyl]-1-butyl-1H-indazole-3-carboxamide
- **Chemical Abstracts index name:** 1H-Indazole-3-carboxamide, N-[1-(aminocarbonyl)-2,2-dimethylpropyl]-1-butyl- (ACI)
- **Other chemical names (page order):**
  - N-(1-Amino-3,3-dimethyl-1-oxobutan-2-yl)-1-benzyl-1H-indazole-3-carboxamide
  - N-(1-Amino-3,3-dimethyl-1-oxobutan-2-yl)-1-benzylindazole-3-carboxamide
  - 2-[(1-Butyl-1H-indazol-3-yl)formamido]-3,3-dimethylbutanamide
  - N-[1-Amino-3,3-dimethyl-1-oxobutan-2-yl]-1-butyl-1H-indazole-3-carboxamide
- **Other names/abbreviations:** ADB-BUTINACA; ADB-BINACA (the page notes this name is also used for the benzyl analogue); ABD-BINACA (as printed in the text)
- **(S)-enantiomer name:** N-[(1S)-1-(Aminocarbonyl)-2,2-dimethylpropyl]-1-butyl-1H-indazole-3-carboxamide
- **(R)-enantiomer name:** N-[(1R)-1-(Aminocarbonyl)-2,2-dimethylpropyl]-1-butyl-1H-indazole-3-carboxamide
- **Trade name:** "ADB-BUTINACA" (sold by Cayman Chemicals as an analytical standard, for the (S)-enantiomer)
- **Street names:** Likely "Spice" (not confirmed for this substance)
- **Code names:** Not given
- **Related metabolites named:** ADB-BUTINACA N-butanoic acid; ADB-BUTINACA N-(4-hydroxybutyl)
- **Molecular formula:** C18H26N4O2 (free base)
- **Molecular weight:** 330.43 g/mol
- **ATC code:** Not given
- **Schedule/control status:** No international controls. Not controlled under any country's national regulations, though it may fall under generic or analogue legislation. A US DEA summary said schedule I, but the page says a Federal Register search did not confirm this.

**(2) Forms and products**

- **Physical form:** The (S)-enantiomer is described as a crystalline solid. Pure material is typically a beige or yellowish powder that blends easily into other drugs.
- **Solubility:** Soluble in dimethylformamide (20 mg/mL), dimethyl sulfoxide (10 mg/mL) and ethanol (20 mg/mL).
- **Formulations/use forms:** Solutions sprayed onto plant material or blotting paper, smoked, vaped (solubilized in a vehicle), or taken orally. Sublingual use is also reported.
- **Product types seen in seizures:**
  - Adulterated cannabis or hemp plant material for smoking
  - Paper infused with the chemical, used mainly to smuggle material into prisons
  - Powders for making formulations and products
- **Product/brand names:** Not given (beyond the analytical standard noted above)
- **Packaging:** Not given
- **Seizure and drug-checking findings:**
  - Detected in seized products or biological samples in 11 countries: Austria, China, France, Republic of Korea, Russian Federation, Singapore, Slovenia, Sweden, Switzerland, United Kingdom and USA.
  - In Scottish prisons (January to June 2021), 76 (60.3%) samples positive, in infused paper.
  - Singapore: 23 cases in biological samples (UNODC Tox Portal).
  - Often found as an adulterant in cannabis, and not the sole substance in many samples.
  - Found in fentanyl-related and heroin-related products (per a public health alert cited on the page).
